page: Microsoft Azure E4pds_v5 is an ARM-based virtual machine belonging to the EPDSv5 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated physical cores and 4 vCPUs powered by an Ampere Altra ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor operating at 3.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is supported by a 154 GB local disk, and the instance is capable of utilizing Premium Storage.

Benchmark results indicate average performance in compute-intensive workloads, with stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests scoring 1822.68 and 7252.56 respectively. However, memory and decompression performance show notable limitations. The PassMark memory score of 1809.89 and the small-block cached read-only memory bandwidth of 283.12 GB/sec are classified as weak. Bzip3 decompression single-threaded performance is poor at 7.4 GB/sec, and multi-threaded decompression is weak at 23.19 GB/sec. Additionally, LLM inference speeds for a small 135M model are poor, processing 151.9 tokens per second for prompts and 41.41 tokens per second for text generation.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E4pds_v5 offers a high memory density relative to its vCPU count, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require high-performance x86 vector extensions or advanced matrix instructions. PassMark database operations scored an average of 2892.68, suggesting suitability for moderate database hosting, caching layers, and memory-intensive applications. However, the weak Redis SET performance of 4.99 million operations per second and weak static web serving throughput of 5.19 GB/sec indicate it is less optimal for high-throughput web serving or real-time key-value stores.
